clips.title: What is Helm in Kubernetes? Helm and Helm Charts explained  | Kubernetes Tutorial 23
clips.why: Nana shows the exact problem a chart solves: many services whose YAML is almost the same, written once as a template with values.
look: The repeated YAML for several microservices that differ only in name, image and version. Our four agent services are that picture.
The template with placeholders, and the values that fill them.
Using the same chart for different environments by changing only the values.
clips.after: Our shared chart is this idea: the gateway, the broker, the worker and the Slack app are one chart with four sets of values.

clips.title: What is Helm in Kubernetes? Helm and Helm Charts explained  | Kubernetes Tutorial 23
clips.why: The folder you get from helm create, file by file, and how values reach the templates.
look: Chart.yaml, values.yaml and the templates folder: the same files you will see in the lab.
How a value can come from values.yaml, from another values file, or from --set on the command line.
That the final values are merged, so you only override what differs.
clips.after: In our units the values come from Terraform, through yamlencode, instead of --set, but they land in the same holes.

clips.title: Learn how to use the Terraform Helm Provider
clips.why: A drawing of how Terraform, its Helm provider and the cluster fit together, before any code.
look: Terraform does not talk to the cluster itself; the Helm provider does, using a kubeconfig.
A Helm chart becomes a resource in Terraform, so it appears in plan and apply like anything else.
Why people manage Helm through Terraform: the same review and state as the rest of the infrastructure.
clips.after: Our infrastructure repo does exactly this for inf: a helm_release per service, planned in a pull request and applied by a person.

practice.q: Finish the template line so the replica count comes from the values.
practice.hint: It is the name used in values.yaml.
practice.why: {{ .Values.replicaCount }} is a hole that Helm fills from values.yaml, or from whatever values you pass in.

practice.q: The chart's values.yaml says replicaCount: 1. The broker's unit passes replicaCount = 2. How many broker pods run after the apply?

options.text: 1, because the chart's own file wins
options.why: values.yaml only holds defaults. Anything you pass in replaces them, the way props replace default props.

options.text: 2, because the values you pass replace the defaults
options.why: Helm merges the values: the defaults first, then yours on top. You only pass what differs.

options.text: 3, because Helm adds the two numbers
options.why: Values are never added together. A value you pass replaces the default with the same name.

practice.q: The broker needs a new image on inf. Put the steps in order.
items: The new broker image is built and pushed to our registry, and its digest is known
The author changes the digest in the broker's unit and runs a plan
The plan, one line out and one line in, is pasted into the pull request
A reviewer approves, and a person applies
Helm records a new revision and the Deployment replaces the pods one by one
practice.why: The change is written down before anything happens, a person reviews and applies it, and the cluster ends with a revision you can point at.

practice.q: tofu apply fails: Service "gateway" exists and cannot be imported into the current release. What happened?

options.text: The chart has a bug in its Service template
options.why: The chart is fine; the same chart works for the broker. The message is about an object that already exists.

options.text: Someone created a Service called gateway by hand, and Helm refuses to take over an object it did not create
options.why: Helm only manages objects with its own labels. Remove the hand-made object so the code becomes the only owner, then apply again.

options.text: Two releases cannot use the same chart
options.why: They can, and that is exactly how all our agent services share one chart.

practice.q: The image line in the broker's unit pins the image so that nobody can change what runs under a known name. What follows the @?
practice.hint: The name of the hash function.
practice.why: A digest is sha256:<hash of the image content>. A tag can later point at other bytes; a digest cannot.
